audience: DriveWealth principal engineers (AI Engineer technical assessment; two 45-minute sessions: live coding + technical deep dive)
core_concepts: reusable AI systems and SDK design
closing_sentence: I don't ask anyone to trust agent output -- every system I build makes the agent prove what it did, and that's exactly the posture regulated financial infrastructure needs.

points.title: Agent graph structure: nodes, state, communication
points.hook: My graphs are frozen contracts before dispatch -- tau.dag_contract.v1 -- so state and topology are validated before any model is called.
points.story: Tau: nodes are handler/join/gate types, state travels as node receipts with an immutable goal hash, communication is receipt-passing not shared mutable state. Compiled DAG is rejected pre-dispatch with named errors.

points.title: Tool call fails, retrieval empty, low-confidence output
points.hook: Every failure gets a failure_code and a recovery packet -- lane-local, never whole-panel; absence is reported, never dropped.
points.story: Ask/Tau: failed lane emits failure_code + recovery_packet_path + next_command; DEGRADED join keeps usable seats. Stage ladder: COMPILED/DISPATCHED/ACKNOWLEDGED/CANDIDATE/SETTLED -- an unadmitted answer cannot read as success.

points.title: Preventing infinite loops and runaway agents
points.hook: Immutable goal hash in every receipt, bounded attempts, and a research rung that is mandatory after two failed attempts -- a third retry from stale context is a guess, and the system refuses it.
points.story: Tau receipts carry the goal hash so drift is detectable; the blocker ledger detects work done BESIDE a wall (avoidance drift); unblock competitions require a proof command that fails now.

points.title: Human-in-the-loop checkpoints and when they trigger
points.hook: Missing required fields fail preflight into an interview packet before any provider is contacted -- the human gate is structural, not polite.
points.story: NEEDS_INTERVIEW: a roundtable without an immutable goal never dispatches. Debugger ladder escalates to the human only for real decisions; complex DAGs are chart-previewed for confirmation before execution.

points.title: Managing multi-step workflow state without chaos
points.hook: State lives in artifacts on disk, one schema per seam, so any run answers 'what happened' the same way -- a roundtable, a competition, and a single call share one projection.
points.story: run dir: dag.json, events.jsonl, per-node receipts, join receipts; status --projection is one normalized read model; handoff.json chains name the next agent.

points.title: Tool/MCP layer versioned independently of the agent graph
points.hook: Skills are versioned capability contracts -- schema-stamped artifacts at every seam mean a tool can evolve behind its contract without touching the graph.
points.story: 340+ skills each with SKILL.md contract (triggers/provides/composes/complies), schema-versioned payloads (v1 suffixes everywhere), scillm gateway isolating provider churn from every consumer.

points.title: Mid-level engineer uses the SDK without understanding internals
points.hook: Every skill has one run.sh front door and a mode router table: user intent to exact command shape. You never need to know which seat is a browser and which is an API.
points.story: Ask quickstart: 'do not invent a custom orchestration path' -- the table maps intent to command; handlers are peers whether browser or API; fail-closed errors name the next command.

points.title: Agent components as reusable primitives across workflows
points.hook: DAG templates are named primitives -- roundtable, compete, creator-reviewer, reflection-loop -- selected by name, not rebuilt per project.
points.story: dag-templates skill catalogs the patterns; composes: frontmatter declares dependencies; the same join-gate primitive serves deliberation panels and isolated competitions.

points.title: Documenting and enforcing standards across a team
points.hook: Standards are executable: best-practices skills are the written contract, agentic evals are the enforcement, and panel-audit turns a prose protocol into a checkable verdict.
points.story: best-practices-roundtable rules became panel-audit code: equal_context, no_silent_consensus, quorum -- 'this run complied' moved from assertion to artifact check.

points.title: Why deterministic checks cover most but not all capabilities
points.hook: Deterministic checks own everything mechanical; judgment work -- visual comparison, quality review -- runs as an agentic second pass, because a pixel-diff proxy for judgment lies confidently.
points.story: Operator-directed rule in the repo: judgment must not be replaced by deterministic proxies; the same wrong assumption can author the code, the fixture, and the assertion.

points.title: Signals tracked per agent run
points.hook: Per node: status, failure_code, requested vs resolved model, requested vs dispatched reasoning effort with downgrade reason, latency segments, response hash -- and model_provenance, because absence of evidence is never confirmation.
points.story: Live-evidence fast solver journals model, effort, latency segments, sha256 per answer; browser receipts record provenance_status confirmed/unconfirmed/mismatch -- a panel cannot claim a tier it cannot prove.

points.title: Measuring whether output is actually grounded
points.hook: Answers are admitted, not assumed: the Sparta chat pipeline gates on answerability before generation and runs an independent verifier after -- and my evidence cards carry source path, line numbers, and content hash.
points.story: spartaChat: answerabilityGate -> memoryAnswerV2Admission -> verifier -> deliveryDecision, toolTrace throughout. Evidence card schema: excerpt, path, line_start/end, content_sha256, freshness.

points.title: Compiler/prover feedback loops (Lean 4)
points.hook: The strongest observability signal is a verifier that cannot be sweet-talked: Lean 4 proofs either compile or they do not, and that binary signal trains the generator.
points.story: lean4-prove: retrieval over 94k exemplars, generation, compilation across 20 parallel silos, retry on failure, GRPO training with compiler rewards. Fintech translation: independent verification of transaction integrity, not model self-report.

points.title: Programmatic PII detection in agent inputs/outputs
points.hook: Detection at the choke points, not policy prose: prompts are preflighted before submission, secrets are redacted debugger-side before capture leaves the process, and purpose policies fail closed.
points.story: browser_prompt_preflight rejects unsafe payloads pre-submit; debugger lane preserves secret redaction end to end; live-evidence session purposes freeze a capability policy digest bound to every artifact.

points.title: Bad output in production on a Tuesday morning
points.hook: I know because a gate trips, not because a user complains -- then diagnosis is a dispatch table, not a war room: the symptom names the one artifact that owns it.
points.story: events.jsonl -> node receipt failure_code -> recovery packet next_command -> drift ledger -> breakpoint only for state nothing wrote down. Every rung produces an artifact before the next starts.

points.title: Why not LangChain/LangGraph/AutoGen; Strands openness
points.hook: My reservation is not fashion: abstraction layers that hide the failure surface make receipts impossible -- I need to own the seam where evidence is admitted. Strands' model-driven loop plus explicit tools is closer to how I already build.
points.story: Tau exists because orchestration IS the product: frozen contracts, receipts, fail-closed gates. A framework is fine when its abstractions are seams you can audit; that is the evaluation lens, not tribal preference.

points.title: DriveWealth domain anchors: SQS events, KYC lifecycle, AutoPilot
points.hook: Your event-driven SQS model is exactly the seam where receipt-gated agents belong: every consumed event leaves a receipt, so reconciliation and audit fall out of the architecture instead of being bolted on.
points.story: Their surface: session-token server-to-server auth, sandbox/UAT by hostname, SQS topics for accounts, orders, positions, KYC status changes, settlements, corporate actions; AutoPilot rebalancing; ACATS; W-8/W-9 and 871(m) tax handling. Agent platform fit: idempotent event consumers with receipts, human-approval gates before any order mutation, PII fencing at KYC document boundaries.

points.title: Mentoring engineers who are not AI specialists
points.hook: Most of this work is logic and precedent, not ML research -- the rigor lives in the platform, so engineers learn contracts and receipts, not transformer internals.
points.story: Mid-level engineers extend the skills library by following the SKILL.md contract and passing the eval gate; the platform enforces what a senior reviewer would have to remember.

diagram_library.note: Prepared phart charts for design-shaped questions; glance the card, open the chart, narrate while redrawing.
